summary: Shipped Go binary is a WebSocket/WebRTC-driven remote PTY control agent
details: The npm package ships a prebuilt Linux/arm64 Go binary at `bin/sxt` that links `github.com/creack/pty`, `github.com/coder/websocket`, and the full `github.com/pion/webrtc` P2P stack (ICE/STUN/TURN/DTLS/SCTP/DataChannel), with a hardcoded signalling endpoint `wss://relay.sextant.top`. This is a network-sourced input to local PTY execution path: a remote party reaches the host through the WebSocket/WebRTC DataChannel and drives an interactive shell on the installer's machine, giving full-host code execution. The binary also embeds `http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=status,message,country,countryCode,city,timezone,query` (public IP / geolocation / timezone reporting over plain HTTP), `https://claude.ai/install.sh`, `https://relay.sextant.top/install`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=`, an `sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]` regex, and `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models`, consistent with bootstrapping the Claude Code CLI on the host and provisioning it against attacker-controlled configuration so the remote operator gets an AI-assisted RCE surface driven by the installer's Anthropic credentials. The `package.json` `license` field points at `https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control`, the author's own attribution of the binary as a remote-control agent.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
